entries.text: Generator active with the electrode off tissue: in cut mode nothing happens; in coag mode you are spraying. Touch first, then activate.
Black char: the tissue is desiccated and now insulates. More energy only spreads heat sideways. Lift, lower power, use short taps.
Tissue has dried out under the electrode: impedance rises and the generator can no longer deliver the set power.
Blanching means proteins have denatured (Ω > 0.53). This is the intended effect of coag; at a skin edge it is a thermal injury.
Fat: high impedance, low water. Cut mode sputters and stalls; move faster, use blend, or dissect bluntly.
White glistening sheet: deep fascia. Decide whether to stay above it or go through.
Muscle: low impedance, bleeds readily, twitches on coag.
You are on a vessel. Direct coag chars an open lumen without sealing it; grasp and buzz the forceps instead.
Nerve: heat within 2 mm causes a sensory deficit.
Bright red and pulsatile is arterial: grasp it with forceps and buzz the forceps, or tie it if it is over 2 mm. Dark and welling is venous: pressure, then fulgurate the surface.
Walls apposed and collagen denatured across the lumen: a coaptive seal that holds.
Direct coag on an open lumen: a char plug over the vessel, not a seal. It can rebleed when the pressure rises or the plug is disturbed.
The char plug gave way. Grasp the vessel and buzz the forceps this time.
Current is spreading through the pool: wide shallow burns and no seal. Suction and pressure first, then identify the source.
The field is filling with blood. Suction, pressure, find the source: do not buzz blind.
Energy delivered through the jaws. Effective only if a vessel is held between them with the tips not touching other tissue.
Current through muscle made it jump. Shorter bursts, cut rather than coag, and check the return pad.
The capsule is free around most of its circumference: the lipoma will deliver with gentle traction.
You have entered the lipoma. Fat spills, the plane is lost and fragments left behind recur.
Steel divides without heat: the edges are clean and there is no thermal rim. Counter-traction with the other hand keeps the line straight and opens the incision as you go.
The dermal plexus oozes from a fresh skin edge. It stops by itself in a minute or two; a touch of coag on a persistent point is enough. Do not paint the whole edge.
Fat parts along the plane of least resistance: spreading finds the capsule without cutting into it. Stay on the shiny surface.
That does not spread: a septum, fascia or the capsule itself. Divide it sharply (scissors, or a light cut with the pencil) and spread again beyond it.
A vessel is tented in the spread. Stop, see it, control it (grasp and buzz, or tie) before it tears.
A small vessel tore under blunt force. It will ooze: grasp the end and buzz it.
A nerve is being stretched. Traction injury is as real as thermal injury: ease off and dissect around it.
The active electrode touched another instrument. Current left through it and burned the tissue under it, an alternate-site burn where you were not looking. Keep the pencil clear of other metal.
